record.paper_title: The average size of a connected vertex set of a graph-Explicit formulas and open problems
record.original_question: For every simple connected graph G of order n, let a_k be the number of connected vertex subsets of G with cardinality k, for k=0,1,2,...,n. Must the sequence (a_0,a_1,...,a_n) always be unimodal, meaning that it never increases again after it has begun to decrease?

evidence.quote: Question 4. For a given simple, connected graph of order n, let ak n k, = 0, 1, 2, …, , denote the number of connected sets of size k. Is the sequence aa a 0 1 , , …, n necessarily unimodal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph of order $n$. A subset $U \subseteq V(G)$ is called a connected (vertex) set of $G$ if the subgraph of $G$ induced by $U$ is connected; by convention, the empty set is considered connected. For each $k \in \{0, 1, 2, \dots, n\}$, let
$$a_k = a_k(G) = \#\{U \subseteq V(G) : |U| = k \text{ and } G[U] \text{ is connected}\}.$$
A finite sequence $(b_0, b_1, \dots, b_n)$ of nonnegative real numbers is called unimodal if there exists an index $m$ such that $b_0 \le b_1 \le \dots \le b_m \ge b_{m+1} \ge \dots \ge b_n$; equivalently, the sequence does not strictly increase at any point after it has strictly decreased.

Question: Is it true that for every simple connected graph $G$ of order $n \ge 1$, the sequence $(a_0(G), a_1(G), \dots, a_n(G))$ is unimodal?
artifact.status_search_result: The unimodality question for the connected-set size sequence of a connected graph appears to remain open in general. Related work (e.g. on random subtrees and unimodal sequences in graphs) has established unimodality for special graph classes such as lollipop graphs, glasses graphs, and theta graphs, but no general resolution—positive or negative—has been located.

status_evidence.title: Random subtrees and unimodal sequences in graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Subtree polynomials of several graph classes (lollipop, glasses, theta) are shown to be unimodal; general question remains.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on unimodality for related connected-substructure sequences; no general resolution.

status_evidence.title: The average size of a connected vertex set of a graph—Explicit formulas and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including the unimodality of the connected-set size sequence.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem.
